nodes.label: Klipper is an in-process Plasma 6 applet embedded in plasmashell, not a separate process
nodes.norm_label: klipper is an in-process plasma 6 applet embedded in plasmashell, not a separate process
nodes.summary: The research brief asked for confirmation that Klipper is a separate process in Plasma 6. The evidence says the opposite: the plasma-workspace applets tree carries applets/clipboard, and the KDE bug archive states the clipboard applet is embedded directly in plasmashell. A standalone klipper source directory still ships, so its presence in the tree is not evidence of a running process. No klipper process runs here and org.kde.plasma.clipboard is absent from the loaded plasmoids, so clipboard history is not being collected and its memory cost is already zero. Reported as a finding, not a confirmation.

nodes.label: kaccess forces QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb and is therefore X11-only
nodes.norm_label: kaccess forces qt_qpa_platform=xcb and is therefore x11-only
nodes.summary: kaccess main.cpp forces QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb before anything else, then verifies the Xlib XKB extension and exits if it does not match. The accessibility daemon therefore runs as an X client under Xwayland inside a nominally native Wayland session, and its functions are sticky keys, slow keys, bounce keys, mouse keys, the bell and a screen-reader toggle. Disabling it on a machine with no assistive-technology user was judged safe; accerciser is the positive control to run before disabling anything.

nodes.label: baloo-widgets is a Dolphin plugin library, not a daemon, so it is not removable dead weight
nodes.norm_label: baloo-widgets is a dolphin plugin library, not a daemon, so it is not removable dead weight
nodes.summary: The brief asked whether baloo-widgets is dead weight when no Baloo widget is loaded. The verdict is not removable: it is a hard dependency of dolphin and a library of Dolphin plugins rather than a daemon, so it costs nothing at runtime. The 352 KiB index under ~/.local/share/baloo is disk residue, not memory; Indexing-Enabled=false plus balooctl6 suspend/disable already leaves the indexer inert, and a baloo_file_cleaner process removes unneeded index files once disabled.

nodes.label: xdg-desktop-portal-gtk must be kept as the documented remedy for GTK font rendering and the on-demand XWayland file chooser
nodes.norm_label: xdg-desktop-portal-gtk must be kept as the documented remedy for gtk font rendering and the on-demand xwayland file chooser
nodes.summary: Running xdg-desktop-portal-gtk alongside xdg-desktop-portal-kde looks like duplication, but the verdict is keep it: it is the documented fix for incorrect GTK font rendering on Plasma and it supplies the on-demand XWayland file chooser. xdg-desktop-portal-kde is itself not removable, exposing 20 portals including file chooser, print and screencast. Upstream forbids xdg-desktop-portal-gnome because it conflicts with the KDE backend, an asymmetry that shows the list is not a dedupe list.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-26 - research-kde-plasma-6-components [ses_f221dc2aaffeD7tR9uzbMitsZ7].md:L16727] The redundant-looking GTK portal was kept because it is the documented remedy, not a duplicate

nodes.label: Savings from thin plasmashell children must be judged by proportional set size, not RSS
nodes.norm_label: savings from thin plasmashell children must be judged by proportional set size, not rss
nodes.summary: The compatibility proxies and other thin children of plasmashell share nearly all their mapped pages with it, so their proportional set size is small and removal frees far less physical memory than the resident set size suggests. The report's closing recommendation was to leave the Plasma core, both portal backends and the greeter alone until proportional-set-size measurement justifies otherwise, rather than acting on RSS figures.

nodes.label: Rewriting a document nearly identically does not reduce its word count; only deletion does
nodes.norm_label: rewriting a document nearly identically does not reduce its word count; only deletion does
nodes.summary: Five successive attempts to hit a 3500-word limit by rewriting the whole file produced 4677, 4104, 4064, 3968 and 3911 words: each pass reproduced the same text with tighter phrasing. The diagnosis recorded in the session is that the problem was not wording but retained sentences, and that the fix had to be surgical deletions of enumerated sentences rather than another rewrite.

nodes.label: Missing rtkit drops PipeWire to RT priority 1
nodes.norm_label: missing rtkit drops pipewire to rt priority 1
nodes.summary: rtkit is not installed on this machine, so PipeWire and WirePlumber log repeated RTKit ServiceUnknown errors and the documented consequence is that MaxRealtimePriority falls back to 1. rtkit 0.14-1, roughly 90 KiB, is in the official Arch extra repository, and the verdict is to install it rather than suppress the warnings.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-26 - research-kde-plasma-6-components [ses_f221dc2aaffeD7tR9uzbMitsZ7].md:L16739] rtkit was to be installed rather than its errors suppressed, because the daemon is what restores RT priority

nodes.label: SDDM's X11 greeter is the documented default for 0.21 while Wayland remains experimental
nodes.norm_label: sddm's x11 greeter is the documented default for 0.21 while wayland remains experimental
nodes.summary: sddm.conf(5) gives DisplayServer a default value of x11, and the Wayland greeter is marked experimental, which is why an Xorg greeter is resident on vt2 despite there being no /etc/sddm.conf. The verdict is to leave it: the X11 greeter is the documented default with the fewest moving parts. Upstream publishes no memory figures for either greeter mode, so no quantitative saving is claimed for switching.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-26 - research-kde-plasma-6-components [ses_f221dc2aaffeD7tR9uzbMitsZ7].md:L14347] The greeter was left on X11 because the Wayland greeter is experimental and upstream publishes no memory figures to justify the switch

nodes.label: /usr owned by an unprivileged user is an escalation surface, not a memory defect
nodes.norm_label: /usr owned by an unprivileged user is an escalation surface, not a memory defect
nodes.summary: The kernel log line systemd-tmpfiles[500]: Detected unsafe path transition /usr (owned by belajarcarabelajar) -> /usr/lib (owned by root) has its root cause in the ownership of /usr rather than in anything tmpfiles does: an intermediate path component owned by a non-root user means tmpfiles refuses to traverse or operate across it. This is the same class as any unprivileged-owned directory in the system path.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-26 - research-kde-plasma-6-components [ses_f221dc2aaffeD7tR9uzbMitsZ7].md:L16741] The /usr ownership entry was kept as a fix because it is a security control, not a memory issue
